A.note: Richest frame. Troop blocks, campfires with smoke, ships in the bay, trees and rocks, and warm light with real depth. The troops are a bit uniform and game-like. The rock is small and far away, and it doesn't read as a fortress.

B.note: Photographic, hazy, desert-like ground, but the frame is almost empty. Faint camp marks on the sand are the only content. No troops, no fort, no siege story. It looks like barren terrain.

C.note: Green plain with grid-like camp patches that read as map tiles or fields. Clumps of dots stand in for troops. Smooth, flat ground, with no clear fortress or ships.

D.note: Similar to C but flatter and paler. The ground is a flat colour field with grid camp rectangles, and the troops are specks. It looks like an unfinished game prototype.

why: A is the only frame with a readable siege (troops, fires, smoke, ships, vegetation, lighting); the others are mostly empty or flat terrain.
top_fix_for_best: Move the camera closer to the fortified rock so it dominates the frame, then add varied troop poses, tents, trenches and earthworks, and cannon smoke over the lines.
